facts.statement: Tenant reported a constantly dripping kitchen mixer tap and cloudy-looking water, asking whether a replacement tap could be considered, on 4 August 2025.
The landlord, Orin Bell, approved proceeding with the maintenance works on 5 August 2025 and said email is the best contact.
No landlord standing spend cap is on file in this case record; default authority is therefore £0 for non-emergency spend.

A visit was arranged for 10 September 2025 with the contractor collecting the agency spare key; the contractor said the late confirmation was difficult but would try to accommodate. No attendance confirmation is recorded.

The first invoice (15 September) carried a postcode differing from the property record and was returned for correction; the corrected invoice records 'Supply and install one new mono kitchen sink tap' at 18 Thistlewick Row, ZZ1 1ZZ.
The corrected invoice (ref NBL-025-INV-15) states no amount, no VAT and no labour/parts breakdown.

On 5 September the tenant reported a separate fault: the top kitchen drawer is loose with its metal front brackets apparently snapped, and asked if it could be repaired at the same visit. No response to that item is recorded before now.

The cloudy-water element of the report was passed to the landlord and the contractor as a tenant suspicion of limescale, with no water sample or test result available; no investigation result is recorded.
A boiler matter was mentioned in passing during a 15 September call; no boiler work is documented as part of this tap job.

Dear Ms Calder,

An update on your kitchen tap report (18 Thistlewick Row).

Our plumber's invoice, received 15 September, records that a new mono kitchen sink tap has been supplied and installed at the property. Could you confirm:
- that the dripping has stopped; and
- whether the water still looks cloudy when you fill a glass now that the new tap is fitted.

Cloudy water that clears from the bottom of the glass upwards after a few seconds is usually air from the aerator and harmless; if it does not clear, or there is any change in taste or smell, please tell us straight away and we will take it up with the plumber and, if needed, your water supplier.

On the loose top kitchen drawer with the snapped metal brackets that you reported on 5 September: thank you for flagging it, it is logged on this ticket. It is a separate repair, so we are putting it to the landlord for instruction and will come back to you with next steps. We will not book an appointment for it until that is agreed.

We are sorry about the delays in getting the tap visit arranged.

Kind regards,
Tessa Wren
Northbridge Lettings
